history.summary: The oldest well-preserved temple in Bhubaneswar, dating to around 650 CE under the Shailodbhavas. Tradition says the sage Parashurama installed the linga here to atone after his campaign against the Kshatriyas — hence the name combining Parashurama and Ishvara. Notable as the first temple with both vimana and jagamohana in the Kalinga idiom, the earliest Odishan temple depicting the eight grahas (not nine), and the earliest representation of the Saptamatrikas in Odisha. Repaired by the British administration in 1903; now ASI-maintained. Coordinates approximate (street-level geocode match in Old Town).

name: Parashurameshvara Temple
town_description: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, is known as the "Temple City of India" for its hundreds of ancient temples from the 7th to 13th centuries, the greatest concentration of Kalinga-style architecture anywhere. Once called Ekamra Kshetra (the mango-forest shrine), it sits on the coastal plain between the Mahanadi delta and the Eastern Ghats. Modern Bhubaneswar is a planned administrative and IT hub built around its ancient old town, home to Lingaraj, Puri's Jagannath pilgrims' transit stop, and Biju Patnaik International Airport.
